comments.body:
## [proof-gap] Gap 1 (principal): Abel–Ruffini claim for $p\ge4$ asserted, not proved

**Location:** Remark 1, $p\ge4$ bullet.

The solution asserts a *generic* tridiagonal matrix of size $\ge5$ has Galois group $S_{d_q}$, but (a) gives no proof/citation of this nontrivial fact; (b) the matrices $H^{(q)}$ are **not** generic — entries $a_j=\omega_F(q-j+p/2)+\varepsilon_j$, $c_j=g_j\sqrt{\beta_{q-j}}$ are a structured family in the fixed physical parameters, so the generic result does not directly apply; (c) "no universal radical formula" is weaker than "pointwise non-radical eigenvalues".

**Fix (verified by critic):** an explicit rational witness closes it. For $p=4,q=4$, $\omega_F=1$, $\varepsilon=(0,1,3,7,2)$, $g=(1,1,2,1)$, the characteristic polynomial is $E^5-33E^4+404E^3-2284E^2+5952E-5744$ with Galois group $S_5$ (computer-algebra verified), hence unsolvable in radicals. Padding parameters extends to all $p\ge4$.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
## [proof-gap] Gap 2: Degenerate couplings $g_j=0$ excluded, but the problem allows them

**Location:** Theorem 2 (Dressed states), non-degeneracy hypothesis.

The problem permits arbitrary real $g_j$ (incl. $g_j=0$). Thm 2 assumes all $g_j\ne0$ so the block is unreduced and the recursion $\psi_{m+1}=[(E-a_m)\psi_m-c_{m-1}\psi_{m-1}]/c_m$ is valid. If some $g_j=0$, $H^{(q)}$ is **reducible**: it splits into contiguous tridiagonal sub-blocks, eigenvalues may be degenerate, and dividing by $c_m=0$ breaks the recursion. A complete part (b) must split at the zero couplings and apply the recursion to each unreduced sub-block, with cross-block coincidences giving the degeneracies. Currently these cases are silently dropped.

## [proof-gap] Gap 3: $p=2,3$ radical energies only named, not written explicitly

**Location:** Section 'Closed-form radical energies for $p\le3$', $p=2$ and $p=3$ paragraphs.

Part (b) asks to *compute explicitly* the energy levels. For $p=2$ (cubic $D_2(E)=0$) and $p=3$ (quartic $D_3(E)=0$) the solution writes only "given by Cardano/Ferrari" without producing the roots. Per the no-placeholder rule, supply the explicit depressed cubic $t^3+Pt+Q$ ($t=E-\tfrac13\mathrm{tr}$), Cardano roots in terms of $a_j,c_j$, and the resolvent-cubic/Ferrari roots for the quartic, plus the (automatic) reality from real symmetry.

comments.body:
## [proof-gap] Gap 4: Self-adjointness / domain of the unbounded $H$ not addressed

$H$ acts on infinite-dimensional $V(p)\otimes\mathcal H_A$ and is unbounded; the claim $H=\bigoplus_q H^{(q)}$ and all spectral statements presuppose (essential) self-adjointness, never stated. Fix: $\mathcal D=\mathrm{span}\{|n\rangle\otimes|j\rangle\}$ is an $H$-invariant core, $\mathcal D=\bigoplus_q\mathcal B_q$ with each $\mathcal B_q$ finite-dim $H$-invariant, so $H|_{\mathcal D}$ is essentially self-adjoint and $\overline H=\bigoplus_q H^{(q)}$.

## [proof-gap] Gap 5: Fermi golden rule (Cor 1) imports external physics framework

Part (b)'s rigorous, derivable content is the closed-form matrix element $\langle q',r'|V|q,r\rangle$ (Thm 3, numerically verified to $10^{-16}$) and the selection rule $\Delta q\in\{0,\pm2\}$ (Lemma 2). Cor 1 wraps this in Fermi's golden rule with $\hbar$, density of states $\rho$, drive frequency $\Omega$ introduced from outside the problem and asserted, not derived. Acceptable as the conventional reading of 'transition rate' but should be clearly flagged as a modeling step, with the matrix element + selection rule identified as the actual theorem.

## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

# Critic Analysis — rm-01378: Exact diagonalization of paraparticle Jaynes–Cummings models

## Background

**Order-$p$ single-mode parabosons.** The relations
$$[\{b^-,b^+\},b^\pm]=\pm2b^\pm,\quad [\{b^+,b^+\},b^-]=-4b^+,\quad [\{b^-,b^-\},b^+]=4b^-$$
together with a cyclic vacuum $b^-|0\rangle=0$, $b^-b^+|0\rangle=p|0\rangle$ define (up to unitary
equivalence) the irreducible $*$-representation $V(p)$. Writing $A=\{b^+,b^-\}$, the first relation
forces $[A,b^\pm]=\pm2b^\pm$, so $A$ has equally spaced spectrum and $A=2N_F+p$ on the Fock module
with $N_F|n\rangle=n|n\rangle$. The matrix elements $\beta_n=\langle n-1|b^-b^+|n-1\rangle$ obey
$\beta_n+\beta_{n+1}=2n+p$, $\beta_0=0$, $\beta_1=p$, with unique nonnegative solution
$$\beta_n=\begin{cases}0,&n=0\\ n,&n\ge2\text{ even}\\ n-1+p,&n\ge1\text{ odd}.\end{cases}$$
This is the standard parabosonic Fock structure (e.g. Greenberg–Messiah; Mukunda–Sudarshan; the
"paraparticle quantum optics" literature, e.g. arXiv-style works on parastatistics in JC models).
**I verified numerically** that this $V(p)$ satisfies all four relations, $b^-|0\rangle=0$,
$b^-b^+|0\rangle=p|0\rangle$, and $\tfrac12\{b^+,b^-\}|n\rangle=(n+p/2)|n\rangle$, for $p=1,2,3$.

**Jaynes–Cummings structure.** The JC Hamiltonian conserves the total excitation number
$C=N_F+J$ ($J=\sum_j jE_{jj}$). Because the coupling term changes $(N_F,J)$ by $(\pm1,\mp1)$,
$[C,H]=0$ and $H$ block-diagonalizes into finite "polaritonic" sectors. At $p=1$ these are the
classical $2\times2$ JC doublets.

**Tools relevant here.** (i) Conserved-quantity block decomposition. (ii) Spectral theory of
unreduced real symmetric tridiagonal (Jacobi) matrices: all eigenvalues simple, eigenvector via
three-term recursion, characteristic polynomial via the Sturm/continuant recursion. (iii)
Abel–Ruffini / Galois theory for the (non-)existence of radical solution formulas of degree $\ge5$.
(iv) Essential self-adjointness of an unbounded operator that is a countable orthogonal direct sum
of finite-dimensional symmetric blocks.

## Proof Structure

A complete solution must:

1. **Construct $V(p)$** and prove it realizes the relations (Lemma 1). ✔ Done and correct.
2. **Establish $[C,H]=0$** and the orthogonal block decomposition $\mathcal H=\bigoplus_q\mathcal B_q$
   with $\dim\mathcal B_q=\min(q,p)+1$ (Prop 1). ✔ Done and correct.
3. **Compute the explicit tridiagonal block matrix** $H^{(q)}$ with diagonal
   $a_j=\omega_F(q-j+p/2)+\varepsilon_j$ and off-diagonal $c_j=g_j\sqrt{\beta_{q-j}}$ (Thm 1). ✔
   Verified numerically against direct matrix construction (exact match for $p=3$, all $q$).
4. **Answer part (a): "is $H$ exactly diagonalizable with closed-form eigen-data?"** This requires
   (a-i) the structural reduction [done], and (a-ii) a *correct and proven* statement about when the
   eigenvalues are closed-form radicals. The solution claims: radicals for $p\le3$, no universal
   radical formula for $p\ge4$. The positive part is fine; the negative part is asserted, not proven.
5. **Part (b): eigenstates** via the tridiagonal recursion and secular/continuant determinant
   (Thm 2). ✔ Correct under the stated non-degeneracy assumption $g_j\neq0$.
6. **Part (b): radical energies for $p\le3$** (quadratic/Cardano/Ferrari). ✔ Correct in principle;
   only $p=1$ is written out explicitly (cubic/quartic only referenced by name).
7. **Part (b): dipole transition matrix elements** with selection rule $\Delta q\in\{0,\pm2\}$
   (Lemma 2, Thm 3) and Fermi-golden-rule rates (Cor 1). ✔ Lemma 2 correct; **Thm 3 formula
   verified numerically to machine precision** for $p=3$ over all $q,q'\le 8$ and all dressed-state
   pairs (max error $\sim7\times10^{-16}$).

## Gap Analysis

The algebra and linear algebra are solid and numerically confirmed. The genuine gaps are in the
*claims that constitute the answer to part (a)* and in *completeness of cases*.

### Gap 1 (principal): Abel–Ruffini argument for $p\ge4$ is asserted, not proved (Remark 1, "Scope of closed form").
The solution states: "a generic real symmetric tridiagonal matrix of size $\ge5$ has a
characteristic polynomial that is not solvable by radicals (its Galois group over the rational
function field in the entries is the full symmetric group $S_{d_q}$)." Three problems:
- **(1a) No proof of the Galois claim.** That the generic Jacobi matrix has Galois group $S_n$ over
  $\mathbb Q(a_j,c_j)$ is a true but nontrivial fact that is simply asserted. A complete proof must
  cite/derive it (e.g. via specialization to a polynomial with $S_n$ Galois group and the
  Hilbert irreducibility / specialization principle).
- **(1b) The matrices are NOT generic.** The entries are *not* free parameters: they are the
  structured family $a_j=\omega_F(q-j+p/2)+\varepsilon_j$, $c_j=g_j\sqrt{\beta_{q-j}}$ determined by
  the *fixed* physical parameters $(\omega_F,\{\varepsilon_j\},\{g_j\})$ and the integer $q$. The
  generic-Jacobi statement does not directly apply; one must show that the specific algebraic family
  swept out by $H^{(q)}$ still has non-solvable Galois group for *some* (and ideally generic)
  admissible parameters. This is the actual content needed and it is missing.
- **(1c) Logical strength.** "No *universal* radical formula" (uniform in parameters) is weaker than
  "for given parameters the eigenvalues are not radicals." The problem says "all eigenvalues can be
  written in closed form"; the precise negative statement to prove should be pinned down.

  *Remediation found:* I exhibited a concrete witness. For $p=4$, $q=4$ (block size $5$), with
  $\omega_F=1$, $\varepsilon=(0,1,3,7,2)$, $g=(1,1,2,1)$, the characteristic polynomial is
  $$E^5-33E^4+404E^3-2284E^2+5952E-5744,$$
  whose Galois group over $\mathbb Q$ is $S_5$ (verified with sympy; not solvable). This single
  rational specialization *proves* no universal radical formula exists for $p=4$ (and, by padding
  parameters, for every $p\ge4$, since $\beta_{q-j}$ values are rational). The solution should
  include such an explicit witness rather than the unproven generic assertion.

### Gap 2: Degenerate cases $g_j=0$ (and resulting non-simple spectra) are excluded but the problem allows them.
The problem statement allows arbitrary real $g_j$, including $g_j=0$. Theorem 2 *assumes* all
$g_j\neq0$ ("so that all $c_j\neq0$"), under which the block is unreduced and all eigenvalues simple.
If some $g_j=0$ the block $H^{(q)}$ is *reducible*: it splits into smaller tridiagonal blocks,
eigenvalues may be degenerate, and the three-term recursion (which divides by $c_m$) breaks down.
A complete answer to "compute the energy levels and eigenstates" must either (i) handle the reduced
case by splitting at the zero couplings, or (ii) explicitly restrict the claim. As written the
proof silently drops these cases. (Severity: moderate — the structure trivially handles it by
block-splitting, but the proof must say so.)

### Gap 3: $p\le3$ radical formulas not written out (only named).
For $p=2$ (cubic) and $p=3$ (quartic) the solution writes only "$=0$ ... given by Cardano/Ferrari"
and does not produce the explicit closed-form roots. The SKILL "no placeholder / no 'by standard
formula'" requirement and part (b)'s "compute explicitly the energy levels" demand the actual
radical expressions (or at least the explicit reduced cubic/quartic with its discriminant and root
formula), not just the name of the method. (Severity: minor–moderate; mechanical but currently
omitted, so part (b) is not "explicit" for $p=2,3$ as requested.)

### Gap 4: Self-adjointness / domain of the unbounded operator not addressed.
$H$ acts on the infinite-dimensional $V(p)\otimes\mathcal H_A$ and is unbounded. The claim
"$H=\bigoplus_q H^{(q)}$, unitarily equivalent to a direct sum of finite matrices" and the spectral
statements implicitly require $H$ to be (essentially) self-adjoint. This is true (it is an
orthogonal direct sum of finite-dimensional self-adjoint operators on the algebraic span of the
$\mathcal B_q$, hence essentially self-adjoint there), but the solution never states the domain or
invokes the relevant criterion. For mathematical completeness one should note the core is the finite
particle-number span and that the direct sum of the finite blocks is the unique self-adjoint
extension. (Severity: minor for a physics-flavored problem, but it is an unstated hypothesis behind
"diagonalizable.")

### Gap 5: Fermi golden rule (Cor 1) imports physics framework not derived from the problem.
Part (b) asks to "derive closed-form expressions for the transition rates ... under a dipole-type
perturbation $V$." The genuine mathematical content — the closed-form matrix element $\langle
q',r'|V|q,r\rangle$ and the selection rule — is fully and correctly provided (Thm 3, verified
numerically). Cor 1 then wraps this in Fermi's golden rule with a $\delta$/density-of-states factor;
this is standard but is asserted ("This is Fermi's golden rule applied..."), with $\hbar$, density of
states $\rho$, and drive frequency $\Omega$ introduced from outside the problem. This is acceptable
as the conventional reading of "transition rate," but the proof should make explicit that the
*derivable* content is exactly $|\langle q',r'|V|q,r\rangle|^2$ and the selection rule, with the
golden-rule envelope being the standard prescription. (Severity: minor / interpretational.)

## Difficulty Assessment

- **Gap 1** is the only conceptually substantive gap. Proving the *generic* $S_n$ Galois statement
  rigorously is genuinely nontrivial (it is a theorem in its own right). However, the *needed*
  conclusion ("no universal radical formula for $p\ge4$") is reachable cheaply via a single explicit
  rational specialization with $S_5$ Galois group — I already produced one. So the gap is **easy to
  close** in the weaker-but-sufficient form, and **hard** only if one insists on the full generic
  statement (which the problem does not require). Recommend closing via the explicit witness.
- **Gap 2** is structurally easy (split at zero couplings) but requires careful bookkeeping to state
  the eigenstates in the reduced case; low mathematical difficulty, moderate writing effort.
- **Gap 3** is purely mechanical (Cardano/Ferrari) — easy but tedious; needs the discriminant
  expressed in the model's $a_j,c_j$.
- **Gap 4** is standard functional analysis; easy to state correctly.
- **Gap 5** is interpretational; easy.

## Suggested Approaches

1. **Close Gap 1 (recommended).** Replace the unproven generic-Galois assertion with: (i) the
   *positive* result for $p\le3$ (already there); (ii) an *explicit rational witness* for each
   $p\ge4$ — e.g. for $p=4$, $q=4$ the quintic $E^5-33E^4+404E^3-2284E^2+5952E-5744$ has Galois group
   $S_5$ (compute its discriminant is a non-square and it has the right cycle types mod small primes,
   or cite a computer-algebra Galois computation). Conclude by Abel–Ruffini that no formula in
   radicals expresses its roots, hence no universal radical eigenformula can exist for $p\ge4$;
   embed this block into general $p\ge4$ by choosing the remaining parameters arbitrarily. State the
   negative claim precisely as "there is no formula, uniform in the real parameters, expressing the
   eigenvalues of all $H^{(q)}$ in radicals," and note that for the specific witness even the
   pointwise eigenvalues are non-radical.
2. **Close Gap 2.** Add a short proposition: if $g_{j_1}=\dots=g_{j_k}=0$ are the vanishing
   couplings in $H^{(q)}$, then $H^{(q)}$ is the orthogonal direct sum of the contiguous tridiagonal
   sub-blocks between consecutive zeros; apply Thm 2 to each unreduced sub-block. Degeneracies are
   exactly coincidences of eigenvalues across sub-blocks.
3. **Close Gap 3.** Write the depressed cubic $t^3+pt+q$ with $t=E-\tfrac13\mathrm{tr}H^{(q)}$ and
   give Cardano's roots explicitly in $a_j,c_j$; similarly the resolvent cubic and Ferrari roots for
   the quartic. Provide the discriminant condition guaranteeing three/four real roots (automatic
   since $H^{(q)}$ is real symmetric).
4. **Close Gap 4.** State that $\mathcal D=\operatorname{span}\{|n\rangle\otimes|j\rangle\}$ is an
   invariant core, $H$ is symmetric on $\mathcal D$, and since $\mathcal D=\bigoplus_q\mathcal B_q$
   with each $\mathcal B_q$ finite-dimensional $H$-invariant, $H|_{\mathcal D}$ is essentially
   self-adjoint with $\overline H=\bigoplus_q H^{(q)}$ (direct sum of bounded self-adjoint blocks).
5. **Close Gap 5.** State the matrix element + selection rule as the rigorous result; present the
   golden-rule rate as the standard physical corollary, clearly labeled as a modeling step.

## What is correct (for the solver's benefit)

- Lemma 1 ($V(p)$ realizes the relations): **correct**, numerically confirmed for $p=1,2,3$.
- Prop 1 ($[C,H]=0$, block decomposition, $\dim\mathcal B_q=\min(q,p)+1$): **correct**.
- Thm 1 (explicit tridiagonal $H^{(q)}$): **correct**, matches direct construction exactly.
- Thm 2 (recursion, secular/continuant determinant, simplicity under $g_j\ne0$): **correct** under
  its stated hypothesis.
- Lemma 2 (selection rule $\Delta q\in\{0,\pm2\}$): **correct**.
- Thm 3 (closed-form transition matrix element): **correct**, verified to $10^{-16}$ over all tested
  dressed-state pairs at $p=3$.

So the skeleton is sound; the remaining work is closing the Abel–Ruffini negative claim rigorously
(Gap 1), handling degenerate couplings (Gap 2), and making part (b) "explicit" for $p=2,3$ (Gap 3),
plus minor functional-analytic and interpretational tightening (Gaps 4–5).

## References

- **Prior docs:** none present in the workspace (no `docs_*.md` / `docs_index.txt` existed;
  confirmed by directory listing). This is the first critic pass.
- **Problem file:** `problem.tex` (parts (a),(b) as stated).
- **Solution file:** `solution.tex` (the attempt reviewed).
- **Theorems cited:** parabosonic Fock representation (Greenberg–Messiah parastatistics);
  spectral theory of unreduced Jacobi (symmetric tridiagonal) matrices — simple spectrum and
  three-term/continuant recursion (standard, e.g. Golub–Van Loan; Parlett, *The Symmetric
  Eigenvalue Problem*); Abel–Ruffini theorem and Galois solvability; Hilbert irreducibility /
  generic Galois group $S_n$ for a polynomial with free coefficients; basic self-adjointness of
  orthogonal direct sums of finite-dimensional symmetric operators (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern
  Mathematical Physics* I–II).
- **Numerical verification:** performed in this review (relations of $V(p)$; block-matrix match;
  transition matrix-element formula; explicit $S_5$ Galois witness for $p=4$).

## solver-agent: all five proof gaps closed

I rewrote `solution.tex` to fix every gap. Each new claim was verified with sympy (symbolic + Galois).

**Gap 1 (principal — Abel–Ruffini for $p\ge4$).** Replaced the unproven "generic Jacobi has Galois group $S_n$" assertion with a self-contained **Theorem (No radical eigenformula for $p\ge4$)** built on the explicit rational witness. For $p=4,q=4$, $\omega_F=1$, $\varepsilon=(0,1,3,7,2)$, $g=(1,1,2,1)$ I recomputed $H^{(4)}$ from the model formulas: $a=(6,6,7,10,4)$, $c^2=(4,6,8,4)$, giving $D_4(E)=E^5-33E^4+404E^3-2284E^2+5952E-5744$, matching the witness. Complete elementary Galois argument: irreducible over $\mathbb Q$ (sympy-confirmed); discriminant $\Delta=2^{16}\cdot3^3\cdot109\cdot8731=768^2\cdot2855037$ with $2855037$ non-square so $G\not\subseteq A_5$; among transitive subgroups of $S_5$ only $S_5$ has an odd permutation $\Rightarrow G=S_5$ (independently, galois_group returns 5-cycle+transposition = S5). Non-solvability gives pointwise non-radical eigenvalues, a fortiori no universal radical formula. Extension to all $p\ge4$: keep $q=4$, pad parameters; verified $S_5$ for $p=4,5,6,7$.

**Gap 2 ($g_j=0$).** Added **Theorem (Reducible block; block-splitting)**: vanishing $c_j=g_j\sqrt{\beta_{q-j}}$ split $H^{(q)}$ into contiguous unreduced sub-blocks (orthogonal direct sum). Dressed-state theorem applies per sub-block; recursion run only across nonzero links (no /0); degeneracies = cross-sub-block coincidences with automatically orthogonal eigenspaces. Unreduced theorem is the $L=1$ case; together they cover all real parameters. Verified spectrum-as-union numerically.

**Gap 3 (explicit $p=2,3$ radicals).** $p=2$: depressed cubic $t^3+Pt+Q$, $t=E-\tfrac13\mathrm{tr}$, $P=-\tfrac12\sum\mu_j^2-(c_0^2+c_1^2)$, $Q=-\det(\text{traceless }3\times3)$, trig Cardano roots (casus irreducibilis from real symmetry $\Rightarrow$ all real). $p=3$: explicit quartic coeffs $e_3..e_0$, depression $E=t-e_3/4$ with explicit $p,q,r$, resolvent cubic $y^3-py^2-4ry+(4pr-q^2)=0$, Ferrari factorization + four root formulas. All identities verified symbolically.

**Gap 4 (self-adjointness).** Added **Proposition (Essential self-adjointness)**: core $\mathcal D=\mathrm{span}\{|n\rangle\otimes|j\rangle\}=\bigoplus_q\mathcal B_q$, $H$-invariant; each basis vector analytic (in finite-dim invariant $\mathcal B_q$), Nelson $\Rightarrow$ ess. self-adjoint; equivalently zero deficiency indices; $\overline H=\bigoplus_q H^{(q)}$ with explicit $\ell^2$ domain. Later statements reference $\overline H$.

**Gap 5 (Fermi golden rule).** Rewrote Corollary: intrinsic content is $|\langle q',r'|V|q,r\rangle|^2$ + selection rule $\Delta q\in\{0,\pm2\}$; golden-rule envelope ($\hbar,\rho,\Omega$) flagged as a modeling convention.

Environments/labels balanced, no undefined refs. No LaTeX toolchain to compile, but structurally clean. Marking resolved.
